title: Visualization of Single Spin-chain Propagation using Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging
authors: Xiaoqian M. Chen, Justin S. Woods, Ulrich Welp, Wai-kwong Kwok, Ralu Divan, David A. Czaplewski, Scott Dhuey, Sujoy Roy, Rajesh V. Chopdekar, Lance E. De Long, Andi Barbour, Claudio Mazzoli, Ian Robinson, J. Todd Hastings
abstract: Domain wall dynamics and their manipulation in finite-size systems serve as a promising platform for beyond Moore's law applications. Yet, the imaging techniques to track their motion in real-space and time are limited. Here, we use magnetic domain walls formed in permalloy artificial square lattice to demonstrate that single-shot Bragg coherent diffraction imaging (BCDI) is a powerful approach for this purpose. Our BCDI reconstructed images revealed milliseconds time-scale dynamics of the antiphase magnetic domain walls traveling through an antiferromagnetically ordered sample.
summary: This work introduces and validates Bragg Coherent Diffraction Imaging (BCDI) as a powerful experimental tool to visualize magnetic domain wall dynamics in artificial spin systems. By analyzing speckle patterns from both structural and magnetic Bragg peaks, the researchers reconstructed real-space images showing domain walls moving over millisecond timescales. This technique offers a significant advancement for studying magnetic materials relevant to next-generation memory applications.
main_problem: The primary goal is to track the motion and dynamics of magnetic domain walls in real-space and time, which is critical for developing next-generation magnetic memory and logic devices.
main_result: The study successfully demonstrated that single-shot Bragg coherent diffraction imaging (BCDI) is a powerful technique to reconstruct real-space movies of domain wall motion on millisecond time scales.
method: The technique uses resonant X-ray scattering via BCDI, which reconstructs real-space images by analyzing speckle patterns at both structural and antiferromagnetic (AF) Bragg peaks simultaneously.
model_or_system: The experiment uses a permalloy artificial square lattice exhibiting an antiferromagnetic (AF) ground state, simulating systems like Artificial Spin Ice (ASI). The measurement is performed using $\sigma$-polarized X-rays to decouple charge and magnetic scattering signals.
key_observables: Reconstructed real-space images showing domain wall motion, magnetic domain phase (color), and lattice structure (amplitude/brightness).
important_parameters: Domain wall dynamics observed on millisecond time scales; lattice reconstruction resolution $\sim 150$ nm; magnetic domain reconstruction resolution $\sim 1.2$ µm.
main_assumptions: The reconstruction assumes a uniform magnetic texture along the z-direction and that the displacement between subsequent time frames is small.
figures_summary: Figures show the time evolution of antiphase domain boundaries via PEEM comparison with simulated speckle patterns (Fig. 1), the scattering geometry (Fig. 2), and the final phase-reconstructed image showing domain walls and their time evolution (Fig. 3 & 4).
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for real-space domain wall tracking, details the BCDI methodology using resonant X-ray scattering and two-step phase retrieval (structural then magnetic), presents the visualization of domain wall dynamics, and discusses future improvements in temporal resolution.
why_interesting: The ability to image magnetic dynamics in real-space and time using X-ray scattering provides a powerful, non-invasive probe into the non-equilibrium dynamics of magnetic textures, which is relevant to understanding phase transitions and energy dissipation in condensed matter systems.

(a)-(h) Single-shot BCDI reconstructed images of AF domains at different time slices in the ’waterfall plot’ – time evolution of the speckle patterns over time (j), whose x-axis is a cut through the AF speckle patterns and y-axis is time evolution.
